triples.relationship: prophetic messages dated in Darius's second year
triples.rationale: Zechariah dates the Lord's word to the eighth month of Darius's second year. Haggai likewise dates a prophetic word to that king's second year, in the sixth month. The shared regnal year places the two messages in the same dated setting while preserving the different months.
triples.source_text: In the eighth month of the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, Berechiah’s son, son of Addo, the prophet, saying:

target_units.text: In the second year under King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying: “Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:

triples.relationship: divine anger after the ancestors reject prophetic messages
triples.rationale: Zechariah recalls the Lord's great anger with the fathers before warning against their example. Chronicles describes the people mocking His prophets until His anger rose without healing, giving a particular account of the rejection and anger recalled by that warning.
triples.source_text: “The Lord was angry with your fathers with great anger.

target_units.text: The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent through prophets, rising early and sending His messengers, because He spared His people and His sanctuary.
They kept sneering at His messengers, treating His words as nothing, and mocking His prophets, until the Lord’s anger rose among His people, until there was no healing.

triples.relationship: shared call to return with a promise of divine return
triples.rationale: Both passages command the people to return to the Lord and promise that He will return to them. Malachi places the same invitation after charges concerning the fathers' injustices and abandoned ordinances.
triples.source_text: You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Return to Me, and I will return to you, says the Lord.

target_units.text: from the injustices of your fathers. You have turned aside from My ordinances and have not guarded them. Return to Me, and I will return to you,” says the Lord Almighty. And you said, “How shall we return?”

triples.relationship: refusal to listen to the former prophets
triples.rationale: Zechariah warns against ancestors who ignored the former prophets' calls to turn from evil. Chronicles likewise describes God's repeated prophetic messages being mocked and His words treated as nothing.
triples.source_text: Do not become like your fathers, against whom the former prophets brought charges, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn away from your evil ways and your evil practices.’ But they did not listen attentively to Me, says the Lord.

target_units.text: The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent through prophets, rising early and sending His messengers, because He spared His people and His sanctuary.
They kept sneering at His messengers, treating His words as nothing, and mocking His prophets, until the Lord’s anger rose among His people, until there was no healing.

triples.relationship: human mortality contrasted with the continuing divine word
triples.rationale: Zechariah asks where the fathers are and whether the prophets live forever, before turning to God's words in the next unit. Isaiah similarly pictures mortal flesh as withering grass while God's word remains forever. The connection preserves the distinction between mortal messengers and their message.
triples.source_text: Your fathers—where are they? And the prophets—surely they will not live forever?

target_units.text: A voice says, “Cry out!” And I said, “What shall I cry?” All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is as the flower of grass.
The grass has withered, and the flower has fallen;
but the word of our God remains for ever.

triples.relationship: prophetic words realized in the ancestors' judgment
triples.rationale: Zechariah recalls words and ordinances overtaking the fathers and the acknowledgment that the Lord acted according to their ways. Chronicles describes deportation and desolation as fulfilling the Lord's word through Jeremiah. Both connect the ancestors' experience with the effective prophetic word.
triples.source_text: Yet receive My words and My ordinances, all that I, in My Spirit, command My servants the prophets, who overtook your fathers.” And they answered and said, “As the Lord Almighty has arrayed Himself to act according to your ways and practices, so He acted toward you.”

target_units.text: He deported the survivors to Babylon, and they became slaves to him and his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,
to fulfill the Lord’s word through Jeremiah’s mouth, until the land accepted its Sabbaths, to keep Sabbath. All the days of its desolation it kept Sabbath, to complete seventy years.

triples.relationship: same-book sequence of dated prophetic revelations
triples.rationale: The opening message is dated to the eighth month of Darius's second year; this vision sequence begins on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month in the same year. The repeated prophet identification and regnal year establish the book's dated progression.
triples.source_text: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month—which is the month Sabat—in the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, Berechiah’s son, son of Addo, the prophet, saying:

target_units.text: In the eighth month of the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, Berechiah’s son, son of Addo, the prophet, saying:

triples.relationship: same-book visions of colored horses between mountains
triples.rationale: The first vision places a mounted man and colored horses between shaded mountains. Chapter 6 presents chariots with colored horses emerging between bronze mountains. The repeated horses-and-mountains scene links the visions, while their colors, vehicles and mountain descriptions remain distinct.
triples.source_text: I saw in the night: look, a man mounted on a flame-red horse! He stood between the two shaded mountains, and behind him were flame-red, gray, dappled and white horses.

target_units.text: I turned and lifted my eyes and saw: look, four chariots coming out from between two mountains! The mountains were bronze mountains.
The first chariot had flame-red horses, and the second chariot black horses,
the third chariot white horses, and the fourth chariot dappled, gray horses.

triples.relationship: same-book request for interpretation of the horse visions
triples.rationale: In both visions Zechariah asks the angel what the presented figures are. Chapter 1 promises an explanation, while chapter 6 supplies one concerning the four winds. The repeated question connects the prophetic vision-and-interpretation pattern without equating all its figures.
triples.source_text: I said, “What are these, lord?” The angel speaking within me said to me, “I will show you what these are.”

target_units.text: I answered and said to the angel speaking within me, “What are these, lord?”
The angel speaking within me answered, “These are the four winds of heaven; they go out to stand beside the Lord of all the earth.

triples.relationship: same-book commission to travel around the earth
triples.rationale: The man explains that the Lord sent these figures to travel around the earth. In chapter 6 the gray horses seek to travel around the earth, receive the command to do so, and carry it out. Both vision scenes expressly describe this commission.
triples.source_text: The man standing between the mountains answered and said to me, “These are the ones the Lord has sent out to travel around the earth.”

target_units.text: and the gray ones were going out and looking to go and travel around the earth.” He said, “Go and travel around the earth!” And they traveled around the earth.

triples.relationship: same-book completion of a journey around the earth
triples.rationale: The first vision's travelers report that they have traveled around all the earth and found it quiet. Chapter 6 likewise reports the commanded travelers going around the earth. The shared completed journey connects the scenes; the report of quiet belongs to chapter 1.
triples.source_text: They answered the angel of the Lord standing between the mountains, “We have traveled around all the earth, and look, all the earth is inhabited and quiet.”

target_units.text: and the gray ones were going out and looking to go and travel around the earth.” He said, “Go and travel around the earth!” And they traveled around the earth.

triples.relationship: seventy years followed by an appeal or promise of restoration
triples.rationale: The angel asks about mercy for Jerusalem and Judah's cities in the seventieth year. Jeremiah promises a divine visitation and return when seventy years for Babylon approach fulfillment. The stated duration and renewed concern for the displaced people connect the passages.
triples.source_text: The angel of the Lord answered, “Lord Almighty, how long wilt Thou refuse mercy to Jerusalem and Judah’s cities, which Thou hast overlooked this seventieth year?”

target_units.text: Because thus said the Lord: When seventy years are about to be fulfilled for Babylon, I will visit you and establish My words for you, to return your people to this place.

triples.relationship: comfort concerning Jerusalem after her distress
triples.rationale: The Lord answers the angel's appeal for Jerusalem with good and comforting words. Isaiah likewise commands comforting God's people and speaking to Jerusalem's heart after her humiliation. Both introduce restoration with an explicit message of comfort.
triples.source_text: The Lord Almighty answered the angel speaking within me with good words and comforting speeches.

target_units.text: Comfort, comfort My people, says God.
You priests, speak to the heart of Jerusalem; comfort her. For her humiliation is fulfilled, her sin is loosed; for from the hand of the Lord she has received double for her sins.

triples.relationship: same-book repeated declaration of jealousy for Jerusalem and Zion
triples.rationale: Both declarations name Jerusalem and Zion and describe the Lord's great jealousy for her. Chapter 8 repeats the earlier assurance while adding great wrath, preserving the book's stated divine concern for the city.
triples.source_text: The angel speaking within me said to me, “Cry out: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy,

target_units.text: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy; with great wrath I have been jealous for her.

triples.relationship: nations blamed for worsening the judgment of God's people
triples.rationale: Zechariah distinguishes the Lord's limited anger from the nations' participation in attacks that brought evils. Isaiah similarly says that God gave His inheritance into the Chaldean power's hand, yet condemns its lack of mercy and excessive burden on the elderly.
triples.source_text: and I am angry with great anger at the nations joining in assault, because I was a little angry, but they joined in attacking to bring evils.

target_units.text: “Sit stricken and enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will certainly no longer be called a kingdom’s strength.
I was provoked against My people; you defiled My inheritance. I gave it into your hand, but you gave them no mercy; you made the elder’s yoke exceedingly heavy.

triples.relationship: the Lord's house in Jerusalem promised and then reported rebuilt
triples.rationale: Zechariah announces the rebuilding of the Lord's house in Jerusalem. Ezra reports the house rebuilt under prophetic encouragement and completed in Darius's sixth year. The link concerns the expressly named rebuilding, without treating the two dated statements as simultaneous.
triples.source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem in compassion, and My house will be rebuilt in her, says the Lord Almighty, and a measure will again be extended over Jerusalem.”

target_units.text: The elders of the Jews and the Levites were building through the prophecy of Haggai the prophet and Zacharias son of Addo. They rebuilt and put it in order by the decree of the God of Israel and by the decree of Cyrus, Darius and Arthasastha, kings of the Persians.
They completed this house by the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.

triples.relationship: same-book renewed favor expressed through Jerusalem's inhabitation
triples.rationale: The Lord promises renewed good for the cities and renewed mercy and choice of Jerusalem. Chapter 8 describes His return to Jerusalem and elderly people and children again occupying her squares, making the promised renewed favor concrete.
triples.source_text: The angel speaking within me said to me, “Cry out: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Cities will again overflow with good things; the Lord will again have mercy on Zion and again choose Jerusalem.”

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: I will return to Zion and dwell within Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the True City, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty a Holy Mountain.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Old men and old women will again sit in Jerusalem’s squares, each holding a staff in hand because of many days.
The city’s squares will be filled with boys and girls playing in her squares.

triples.relationship: horns interpreted as political powers in prophetic visions
triples.rationale: Zechariah sees four horns, identified in the following unit with powers that scattered Judah and Israel. Daniel interprets ten horns as ten kings. Both visions use horns for political powers, while the numbers and identified actions differ.
triples.source_text: I lifted my eyes and saw: look, four horns!

target_units.text: As for the kingdom’s ten horns, ten kings will arise, and another king will arise after them. He will surpass the earlier ones in evils and humble three kings.

triples.relationship: same-chapter explanation of the horns' scattering of Judah and Israel
triples.rationale: The angel first identifies the horns as those that scattered Judah and Israel. The later explanation repeats their scattering of Judah and shattering of Israel and describes nations lifting a horn against the Lord's land. The repeated charge gives the vision its stated national setting.
triples.source_text: I said to the angel speaking within me, “What are these, lord?” He said to me, “These are the horns that scattered Judah and Israel.”

target_units.text: I said, “What are these coming to do?” He said to me, “These horns that scattered Judah also shattered Israel, and none of them lifted a head. These entered to sharpen them for their hands—the four horns, the nations lifting a horn against the Lord’s land to scatter it.”

triples.relationship: visionary surveyor carrying measuring equipment
triples.rationale: Zechariah sees a man with a land-measuring cord before the explanation that he will measure Jerusalem. Ezekiel likewise sees a man carrying a builders' cord and measuring reed within a vision of a city-like structure and its enclosure. Both present a surveyor with explicit measuring equipment.
triples.source_text: I lifted my eyes and saw: look, a man with a land-measuring cord in his hand!

target_units.text: in a vision of God into Israel’s land and set me upon a very high mountain. Upon it, opposite, was something like a city’s structure.
He brought me in there, and behold, a man whose appearance was like gleaming copper. In his hand were a builders’ cord and a measuring reed, and he stood at the gate.

The man said to me, ‘Have you seen, son of man? See with your eyes, hear with your ears and set in your heart everything I show you, for you have entered here so that it might be shown to you. You will show Israel’s house everything you see.’

Behold, an enclosure surrounded the house outside. In the man’s hand was a reed measuring six cubits by the cubit and handbreadth. He measured the outer wall: its width equaled the reed, and its height equaled the reed.

triples.relationship: same-book promised measuring of Jerusalem enacted in a vision
triples.rationale: The earlier promise says a measure will again extend over Jerusalem. The man now states that he is going to measure Jerusalem's width and length. The shared city and measuring action connect promise and visionary scene.
triples.source_text: I said to him, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide it is and how long.”

target_units.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem in compassion, and My house will be rebuilt in her, says the Lord Almighty, and a measure will again be extended over Jerusalem.”

triples.relationship: restored inhabitation with multiplied people and animals
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises Jerusalem's fruitful inhabitation because of many people and animals. Ezekiel likewise promises inhabited cities and multiplied humans and livestock upon Israel's mountains. Both explicitly combine restored settlement with human and animal abundance.
triples.source_text: and said to him, “Run and speak to that young man: Jerusalem will be inhabited fruitfully because of the multitude of people and animals within her.

target_units.text: I will multiply people upon you, all Israel’s house completely. The cities will be inhabited and the devastated land rebuilt.
I will multiply humans and livestock upon you, settle you as at your beginning and do you good as in your former times. You will know that I am the Lord.

triples.relationship: divine protection of Zion pictured with fire and glory
triples.rationale: Zechariah promises that the Lord will be Jerusalem's surrounding wall of fire and glory within her. Isaiah describes cloud, the light of burning fire and glory over Zion, followed by shelter from harsh conditions. Both join fire and glory with protection, using different protective images.
triples.source_text: I will be a wall of fire around her, says the Lord, and I will be glory within her.”

target_units.text: He will come, and it will be: a cloud will shade every place of Mount Zion and everything around her by day, and as of smoke and as of a light of fire burning by night; with all the glory it will be covered.
It will be shade from heat, shelter and concealment from harshness and rain.

triples.relationship: the Lord surrounding His people in Jerusalem's setting
triples.rationale: The Lord promises to surround Jerusalem as a wall of fire. The psalm compares the mountains around Jerusalem with the Lord around His people. Both portray His surrounding protection, without making the psalm's mountains a literal fiery wall.
triples.source_text: I will be a wall of fire around her, says the Lord, and I will be glory within her.”

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. Those trusting in the Lord are like Mount Zion; the one dwelling in Jerusalem will never be shaken.
Mountains are around her, and the Lord is around His people, from now and for ever.

triples.relationship: divine gathering from the reaches of dispersion
triples.rationale: Zechariah joins the call to flee the northern land with God's promise to gather from the four winds of heaven. Deuteronomy promises gathering from the nations and even from one end of heaven to the other. Both describe divine recovery from extensive dispersion.
triples.source_text: “Oh! Oh! Flee from the northern land,” says the Lord, “because I will gather you from the four winds of heaven,” says the Lord.

target_units.text: then the Lord shall heal your sins, and have mercy upon you, and shall gather you again from all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you.
If your dispersion is from one end of heaven unto the other end of heaven, from thence shall the Lord your God gather you, and from thence shall the Lord your God take you.
And the Lord your God shall bring you into the land which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it; and He shall do you good, and make you more numerous than your fathers.
